newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean forex reserves fall to 20-month low - paper.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean forex reserves fall to 20-month low - paper.

text.p: South Korea's foreign exchange reserves fell to the lowest level in 20 months in February due to a swelling current account deficit and slowing fund influx from abroad, the Chosun Ilbo newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The report quoted the Bank of Korea as saying the reserves stood at $29.8 billion at the end of February, the lowest level seen since June 1995 when reserves were $28.3 billion.
South Korea's foreign exchange reserves continued to fall after the figures hit a record $36.5 billion at the end of June last year, the report said.
Officials at the central bank could not immediately be reached for comment.
"The reserves have been falling due to increasing current account deficit and declining capital influx from abroad," a senior official at the bank was quoted as saying.
The central bank said on Tuesday South Korea's current account deficit widened $3.09 billion in January, almost double the $1.72 billion shortfall a year earlier.
South Korea has blamed falling international prices of key export items, including dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips, and the yen's steep depreciation for the huge shortfall.
The Finance and Economy Ministry has forecast this year's current account deficit at about $18 billion, compared with a $23.72 billion shortfall in 1996.
